UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user profile within the CampusConnect application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user profile.

socialLinks.description: An array of social media links associated with the user (LinkedIn, LeetCode, GitHub, etc.)

role.description: User's role within the campus community (e.g., student, faculty, HOD).

profileImageUrl.description: URL of the user's profile image.

Announcement.title: Announcement
Announcement.description: Represents an announcement posted on the announcement dashboard.

attachments.description: An array of URLs pointing to attached documents, images, or videos.

scheduledAt.description: The date and time the announcement is scheduled to be posted.

Event.title: Event
Event.description: Represents an event (workshop, tech talk, hackathon) in the integrated events section.

startTime.description: Date and time the event starts.

endTime.description: Date and time the event ends.

registeredUserIds.description: References to UserProfiles. (Relationship: Event N:N UserProfile)

ForumPost.title: ForumPost
ForumPost.description: Represents a post in the discussion forum.

id.description: Unique identifier for the forum post.

createdAt.description: Date and time the post was created.

Resource.title: Resource
Resource.description: Represents a resource (notes, papers, materials) in the resource hub.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to ensure security, scalability, and ease of debugging, following the principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, and DBAC. User profiles are stored in `/users/{userId}` using Path-Based ownership, guaranteeing that only the user (or admins) can access their own profile data. Announcements, ForumPosts and Resources are stored in collections `/announcements`, `/forumPosts`, and `/resources` respectively with denormalized `authorId` or `uploaderId` fields to enable efficient querying and listing of posts by a specific user. Events are stored in the `/events` collection. To manage event registrations, a subcollection `/events/{eventId}/registrations/{userId}` is used, which simplifies checking if a user is registered for an event. This structure avoids `get()` calls in security rules, enabling atomic operations and clear rule definitions. Global roles are managed via document existence in dedicated collections (e.g., `/roles_admin/{uid}`), simplifying role-based access control. The structure facilitates secure `list` operations by segregating data based on access requirements and using denormalized authorization fields.
